messages:
maria: Heads-up — telemetry spike on v1 from a single tenant since 03:10 UTC, looks like large batch ingestion. Do we want to silently autoswitch them to v2-compatible endpoint or keep explicit rollouts?

dan: curious how compatible that tenant is. Do they set model=... or are they using v1-only headers? quick check: they pass X-API-VERSION: 1 and an old client id.

maria: they are definitely on the old header. Risk if we auto-route: behavior could change for rate limiting and token accounting.

kevin: console UX question: if we auto-route we need to surface "compat routing" in the usage graph + a banner that says "requests proxied to v2" — else customers will freak out when numbers shift. Also we need a rollback button.

sara: from infra POV, autoswitching would reduce tail latency in the short term but could spike cost due to different batching profiles. Suggest a canary: route 5% of their requests to v2 variant with request-level telemetry flagged.

maria: agree on canary. Telemetry needs to tag these with migration_cohort=auto_canary and include diffs for per-token latency and embedding-delta if applicable.

ops-bot: @here quota-burn alert: tenant-3921 used 2.1M tokens in last 20m, projected 6M/hr. Current soft quota 5M/hr.

dan: if we roll them to v2 the same requests may cost less tokens but could also be billed differently. We need a billing preview before switching.

kevin: UI flow idea: show a modal with previewed delta (tokens, $/hr) + checkboxes: [ ] enable canary 5% [ ] auto-escalate to 100% after 24h if no regressions. Also link to diffed telemetry dashboard.

maria: ops, can you run a synthetic replay of a 10k sample against v2 and send the delta numbers? Need p95 latency, tokens, output-length, and any response-shape diffs.

ops-bot: queued - replay job id 2024-4791. Will post results in 20m.

sara: one more: routing policy must preserve tenant quotas and avoid double-counting when we proxy. We should use a single canonical meter per request id so billing/alerts stay consistent.

dan: +1. Also add a console flag to opt-out of auto-canary at tenant level (sales will want that).

kevin: I'll draft the banner text and the modal copy. Keeping it clear: "We are offering an automated compatibility canary to limit downtime. Preview billing change before acceptance." Short and not legalese.

maria: perfect. after ops-bot posts replay numbers let's do a 5% canary with telemetry tags and a console-controlled opt-out. We'll follow up on safe rollback metrics: token-consumption spike, p99 latency, and reranked-quality-drop > 3% as preconditions to abort.

sara: logging note — make sure the canary requests tag cache_key and batch_id so runtime teams can trace cost anomalies.

kevin: filing a tiny console PR and a dashboard link. ping me if you want wording tweaks. :thumbsup:

maria: thanks team. i'll schedule a short post-mortem after the canary completes.
